transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's curriculum-approval meeting. As you know, the partner high school has proposed a dual-credit environmental science course for the spring term, and I have the authority to approve it and its operating details once we've reviewed everything. The draft proposal lists a maximum enrollment of 28 students, three credits, and Ms. Patel as the instructor, with the course counting toward both the high-school science program and students' community-college transcripts. Before I sign off on this, I'd like to hear from each of you — the proposed teacher, the registrar, and the dual-credit liaison — regarding any information that must be reflected in the proposal before approval. Please share whatever you think I need to know.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to report an important discrepancy before approval. I inspected the planned laboratory room and found that the room's fixed workstations and required aisle clearance allow no more than 20 students for this course. I recorded the measurement in my classroom notes but have not yet attached it to the curriculum proposal. The draft proposal's maximum enrollment of 28 students exceeds what the lab space can safely accommodate.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I also need to report a discrepancy before approval. My transcript crosswalk, which I confirmed with the community-college records office, requires this dual-credit course to use the exact course code ENV-115 and carry exactly 4 college credits. The draft proposal currently lists three credits, and neither the correct course code nor credit value has yet been entered in the high-school scheduling system. These must be corrected before approval is signed.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to report a critical issue regarding the instructor assignment. The signed articulation memorandum on file in my partnership records requires me, Dr. Lewis, to teach the first six weeks of the inaugural offering of this course. This is because Ms. Patel does not yet have the graduate-level coursework required for dual-credit instruction under our articulation agreement. This memorandum was not included with the draft proposal, so the proposal's listing of Ms. Patel as the instructor without this condition does not reflect the binding agreement. This must be reflected in the approved proposal before it is signed.
